title: Chief Minister, State Council of Ministers and State Legislature

faqs.q: In the parliamentary system of government, the Chief Minister represents which kind of executive authority?
faqs.e: The Governor is the de jure (nominal) executive, while the Chief Minister is the de facto (real) executive.

faqs.q: The position of the Chief Minister at the state level is analogous to which position at the Centre?
Which Article of the Constitution provides that the Chief Minister shall be appointed by the Governor?
When no party has a clear majority in the assembly, the Governor usually asks the appointed Chief Minister to seek a vote of confidence within what period?
A person who is not a member of the state legislature can be appointed Chief Minister for a maximum of how long before being elected to the legislature?
A Chief Minister may be a member of which House(s) of the state legislature?

options.b: Neither House, since the Chief Minister need not be a legislator
options.c: Either the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council

faqs.a: Either the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council

faqs.q: As per Sarkaria Commission recommendations, if a single party has an absolute majority in the Legislative Assembly, who should automatically be asked to become Chief Minister?

Consider the following statements regarding the Sarkaria Commission's order of preference for selecting a Chief Minister when no single party has a majority:
(I) An alliance of parties formed prior to the elections
(II) The largest single party staking a claim with the support of others, including independents
(III) A post-electoral coalition of parties, with all partners joining the government
Which of the above is/are part of the recommended order of preference?
As per the Sarkaria Commission, a Chief Minister who is not the leader of a party with absolute majority should seek a vote of confidence within how many days of taking over?
As per the Sarkaria Commission, when rival claims to majority support are contested before the Governor, what is the prudent course of action?

options.a: The rival claims should be tested on the floor of the House
options.b: The Governor should dissolve the assembly
options.c: The Governor should personally verify support through written affidavits
options.d: The Governor should refer the matter to the President

faqs.a: The rival claims should be tested on the floor of the House

faqs.q: Before entering office, the Chief Minister is administered which two oaths by the Governor?

options.a: Oath of office and oath of allegiance
options.b: Oath of office and oath of secrecy
options.c: Oath of secrecy and oath of confidentiality
options.d: Oath of allegiance and oath of secrecy

faqs.a: Oath of office and oath of secrecy

faqs.q: The term of the Chief Minister is not fixed and he/she holds office during whose pleasure?
In which case did the Supreme Court rule that a Chief Minister cannot be dismissed by the Governor as long as he/she enjoys majority support in the assembly?
faqs.e: Decided in 1994; despite this ruling, there have been instances of governors dismissing Chief Ministers without giving them an opportunity to prove majority.

faqs.q: The salary and allowances of the Chief Minister are determined by whom?
The Governor appoints only those persons as ministers who are recommended by whom?
Whose resignation or death automatically dissolves the entire council of ministers?
faqs.e: The resignation or death of any other minister merely creates a vacancy, which the Chief Minister may or may not choose to fill.

faqs.q: Which Article specifically deals with the Chief Minister's duty to communicate Council of Ministers' decisions to the Governor?
The Chief Minister advises the Governor on the appointment of which of the following officials?

options.d: Advocate General, State Public Service Commission members, and State Election Commissioner

faqs.a: Advocate General, State Public Service Commission members, and State Election Commissioner

faqs.q: Who can recommend the dissolution of the legislative assembly to the Governor at any time?
The Chief Minister acts as the chairman of which body?
The Chief Minister acts as vice-chairman of the concerned zonal council by rotation, holding office for what period at a time?
faqs.e: The Union Home Minister is the chairman of all the zonal councils.

faqs.q: The Chief Minister is a member of the Inter-State Council and the Governing Council of NITI Aayog, both of which are headed by whom?
Which Article provides that ministers shall hold office during the pleasure of the Governor and that the Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the legislative assembly?

Which Article deals with the rights of Ministers as respects the Houses of the state legislature?
This chapter is dense (Articles 163/164/166/167/177, composition, cabinet, cabinet committees) — estimated around 40-45 atomic questions, within the single-batch threshold.
faqs.e: See table below for the full set of Articles related to the Chief Minister.

rows: Council of Ministers to aid and advise Governor
Conduct of business of the Government of a State
Duties of Chief Minister as respects furnishing information to Governor
Rights of Ministers as respects the Houses

faqs.q: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the status of the Council of Ministers to aid and advise the Governor?
Which Article deals with the appointment, tenure, responsibility, qualifications, oath, and salaries of ministers?
As per Article 163, the advice tendered by Ministers to the Governor shall be enquired into by which authority?
Which Amendment Act excluded Bihar from the requirement of having a tribal welfare minister?
faqs.e: Bihar was excluded as it has no Scheduled Areas and a very small Scheduled Tribes population; the same Amendment extended the provision to Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand.

faqs.q: Which Amendment Act limited the total number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, to 15 per cent of the total strength of the legislative assembly?
As per the 91st Amendment Act, the minimum number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, in a state shall not be less than what?
The 91st Amendment Act, 2003 also disqualified a member of the state legislature from being appointed a minister if disqualified on which ground?
A minister who is not a member of the state legislature must become a member of either House within how many consecutive months, failing which he/she ceases to be a minister?
As per Article 166, all executive action of the Government of a State shall be expressed to be taken in whose name?
Under Article 166, who makes rules for the allocation of business among ministers, except where the Governor is required to act at discretion?
Which Article lays down the duty of the Chief Minister to communicate all Council of Ministers' decisions to the Governor?
As per Article 177, every minister has the right to speak and take part in proceedings of the Assembly and Council, but is not entitled to what?
In which case did the Supreme Court hold that the Governor must act on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers except in matters of discretion?
faqs.e: Decided in 1974; the Court held that wherever the Constitution requires the Governor's satisfaction, it means the satisfaction of the Council of Ministers, not the Governor's personal satisfaction.

faqs.q: The other ministers, apart from the Chief Minister, are appointed by the Governor on whose advice?
A minister who is a member of one House of the state legislature can speak in the other House but may vote only in which House?

options.a: The House of which he/she is a member

faqs.a: The House of which he/she is a member

faqs.q: Before entering office, a minister is administered which two oaths by the Governor?

options.a: Oath of allegiance and oath of secrecy
options.b: Oath of office and oath of secrecy
options.c: Oath of secrecy and oath of confidentiality
options.d: Oath of office and oath of allegiance

faqs.a: Oath of office and oath of secrecy

faqs.q: The salaries and allowances of ministers are determined by whom?
Which fundamental principle underlies the working of the parliamentary system, as stated under Article 164?
When the legislative assembly passes a no-confidence motion against the Council of Ministers, which ministers are required to resign?

options.c: All ministers, including those from the legislative council
options.d: Only ministers from the legislative assembly

faqs.a: All ministers, including those from the legislative council

faqs.q: Under the principle of individual responsibility, the Governor can remove a minister only on whose advice?
Is there a constitutional provision for legal responsibility of ministers in the states, requiring countersignature of a Governor's public act order?

options.a: No, there is no such provision

faqs.a: No, there is no such provision

faqs.q: Who determines the size of the state Council of Ministers and the ranking of ministers, since the Constitution does not specify this?

Consider the following statements regarding the categories of ministers in a state Council of Ministers:
(I) Cabinet ministers head important departments and attend cabinet meetings
(II) Ministers of state are always members of the cabinet
(III) Deputy ministers are not given independent charge of departments
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: Ministers of state are not members of the cabinet and do not attend cabinet meetings unless specially invited.

faqs.q: Deputy Chief Ministers, when included in the Council of Ministers, are appointed mostly for what reason?
Which smaller body, consisting only of cabinet ministers, is described as the real centre of authority in the state government?
The Cabinet is described as an advisory body to whom?
Cabinet committees are of how many types?
faqs.e: They are of two types — standing (permanent) and ad hoc (temporary).

faqs.q: Cabinet committees are set up by whom, causing their number, nomenclature, and composition to vary over time?
Decisions taken by cabinet committees can be reviewed by which body?
The term "ministry" or "ministries," referring to divisions of government, is used at which level of government in India?
faqs.e: The state government is divided into departments, not ministries.

faqs.q: Which Article deals with the conduct of business of the Government of a State?
faqs.e: See table below for the full set of Articles related to the State Council of Ministers.

rows: Council of Ministers to aid and advise Governor
Conduct of business of the Government of a State
Duties of Chief Minister as respects furnishing information to Governor
Rights of Ministers as respects the Houses

faqs.q: Which range of Articles in Part VI of the Constitution deals with the organisation, composition, duration, officers, procedures, privileges and powers of the state legislature?
As of the current position described in the text, how many states have a bicameral legislature?
faqs.e: These are Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra and Karnataka.

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding legislative councils in Indian states:
(I) The Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Council was abolished by the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019
(II) The Tamil Nadu Legislative Council Act, 2010 has come into force and is operational
(III) The Legislative Council in Andhra Pradesh was revived by the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council Act, 2005
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: The Tamil Nadu Legislative Council Act, 2010 has not come into force.

faqs.q: Which Amendment Act provided for a Legislative Council in Madhya Pradesh, though it has never actually been notified?
faqs.e: A notification to this effect must be made by the President, but so far none has been made, so Madhya Pradesh continues to have only one House.

faqs.q: In a unicameral state, the state legislature consists of the Governor and which other component?

options.a: Neither, since the Governor alone constitutes it
options.c: Both the legislative council and assembly

faqs.q: The legislative council, being the upper house, is also known as the house of elders and is referred to in Hindi as what?
Which Article of the Constitution provides for the abolition or creation of legislative councils in states?
To abolish or create a legislative council, the concerned state legislative assembly must pass a resolution by what kind of majority?
faqs.e: This requires a majority of the total membership of the assembly and a majority of not less than two-thirds of members present and voting.

faqs.q: Is the Parliament's Act under Article 169 abolishing or creating a legislative council deemed to be a constitutional amendment for the purposes of Article 368?

options.a: Yes, it always requires the Article 368 procedure
options.b: No, it is passed like an ordinary piece of legislation
options.c: Only when a bicameral state is involved
options.d: Only when creating a council, not abolishing one

faqs.a: No, it is passed like an ordinary piece of legislation

faqs.q: In which year was the Legislative Council of Andhra Pradesh originally created, before its later abolition and revival?
In which year was the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council abolished, prior to its 2007 revival?
The legislative councils of Punjab and West Bengal were both abolished in which year?
What is the maximum strength fixed for a state legislative assembly?
What is the minimum strength fixed for a state legislative assembly under the general rule?
In case of Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim and Goa, the minimum strength of the legislative assembly is fixed at what number?
The minimum strength of the legislative assembly is fixed at 40 for Mizoram and at what number for Nagaland?
The provision for nomination of one member from the Anglo-Indian community to the state legislative assembly ceased to have effect on which date?
faqs.e: The 104th Amendment Act, 2019 discontinued the extension of this provision, which had last been extended up to 2020 by the 95th Amendment Act, 2009.

faqs.q: For the purpose of holding direct elections to the assembly, each state is divided into what?
The demarcation of territorial constituencies ensures uniformity of what, throughout the state?

options.c: Number of polling booths per constituency
options.d: The ratio between population of each constituency and seats allotted to it

faqs.a: The ratio between population of each constituency and seats allotted to it

faqs.q: Which Amendment Act froze the total number of seats in each state's assembly and its division into territorial constituencies at the 1971 level, till the year 2000?
The 84th Amendment Act of 2001 extended the ban on readjustment of assembly seats up to which year?
Which Amendment Act provided that delimitation of constituencies would be done on the basis of the 2001 census rather than the 1991 census, without altering the total number of seats?
Under the 104th Amendment Act of 2019, reservation of seats for SCs and STs in state legislative assemblies is set to last until which year?
What is the maximum strength of a state legislative council, expressed as a fraction of the assembly's total strength?
What is the minimum strength fixed for a state legislative council?
Though the Constitution fixes the maximum and minimum limits for a legislative council's strength, its actual strength is fixed by whom?
Of the total members of a legislative council, what fraction is elected by members of local bodies such as municipalities and district boards?
What fraction of legislative council members is elected by graduates of three years' standing residing within the state?

What fraction of legislative council members is nominated by the Governor from persons with special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art, cooperative movement and social service?
Members of a legislative council are elected in accordance with which electoral system?

options.d: Proportional representation by single transferable vote

faqs.a: Proportional representation by single transferable vote

faqs.q: Among the states, which has the highest number of seats in its legislative assembly?
faqs.e: See table below for the strength of legislative assemblies and councils and SC/ST reserved seats across major states.

faqs.q: What is the normal term of the state legislative assembly from the date of its first meeting after general elections?
The term of the legislative assembly can be extended during a national emergency by a law of Parliament, for how long at a time?
faqs.e: This can be done for any length of time, but the extension cannot continue beyond six months after the emergency ceases to operate.

faqs.q: After a national emergency ceases to operate, within how many months must the extended assembly be re-elected?
Is the state legislative council, like the Rajya Sabha, subject to dissolution?

options.a: No, it is a permanent body not subject to dissolution
options.c: No, but it is subject to prorogation only once a decade

faqs.a: No, it is a permanent body not subject to dissolution

faqs.q: What fraction of legislative council members retire on the expiration of every second year?
faqs.e: This means a member of the council continues in office for six years.

faqs.q: Vacant seats in the legislative council arising from retirement are filled by fresh elections and nominations at the beginning of every which year?
What is the minimum age prescribed for a person to be chosen as a member of the legislative council?
What is the minimum age prescribed for a person to be chosen as a member of the legislative assembly?
As per the Representation of the People Act, 1951, a person to be qualified for the Governor's nomination to the legislative council must satisfy which additional requirement?

options.b: Be a member of a recognized political party
options.c: Have five years of political experience
options.d: Be a resident in the concerned state

faqs.a: Be a resident in the concerned state

faqs.q: Under the Constitution, a person is disqualified from being a member of the state legislature if he/she holds any office of profit under the Union or state government, except which office?

options.d: Chairman of the Public Service Commission

faqs.q: Which of the following is a constitutional ground for disqualification of a member of the state legislature?

options.c: Being of unsound mind and so declared by a court
options.d: Failure to attend more than 30 days of sittings

faqs.a: Being of unsound mind and so declared by a court

faqs.q: Under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, conviction for an offence resulting in imprisonment for how many years or more results in disqualification?
faqs.e: However, detention of a person under a preventive detention law is not a disqualification.

faqs.q: Under the Representation of the People Act, a person is disqualified if they are a director or managing agent, or hold an office of profit, in a corporation in which the government has at least what percentage of share?
On the question of whether a member has become subject to disqualification, whose decision is final?
faqs.e: However, the Governor must obtain the opinion of the Election Commission and act accordingly.

faqs.q: Disqualification on the ground of defection is governed by which Schedule of the Constitution?
The question of disqualification on the ground of defection for a member of the legislative assembly is decided by whom?
In which case did the Supreme Court rule that the Speaker/Chairman's decision on disqualification under the Tenth Schedule is subject to judicial review?
faqs.e: Decided in 1992.

faqs.q: Every member of either House of the state legislature must make and subscribe to an oath or affirmation before whom, before taking their seat?

options.a: The Governor or a person appointed by him/her
options.c: The Chief Justice of the state High Court

faqs.a: The Governor or a person appointed by him/her

faqs.q: What is the daily penalty for a person who sits or votes as a member in a House before taking the prescribed oath?
If a person is elected to both Houses of the state legislature simultaneously, what happens to their membership?

options.a: The Governor decides which seat they retain
options.b: They automatically remain a member of only the assembly
options.c: Their seat in one of the Houses falls vacant as per state legislature's law
options.d: They must resign from the state legislature entirely

faqs.a: Their seat in one of the Houses falls vacant as per state legislature's law

faqs.q: A member's seat can be declared vacant by the House if he/she is absent from all its meetings for a period of how many days without permission?
A member's resignation from a House takes effect and the seat falls vacant when what occurs?

options.c: The resignation is accepted by the Speaker/Chairman

faqs.a: The resignation is accepted by the Speaker/Chairman
faqs.e: The Speaker/Chairman need not accept the resignation if not satisfied that it is voluntary or genuine.

faqs.q: Among the "other cases" of vacation of seat, a member must vacate his/her seat in the state legislature if elected to which office?

options.a: Chief Justice of a High Court

faqs.q: A member of the state legislature must also vacate his/her seat if appointed to which office?

options.d: Chairman of the State Public Service Commission

faqs.q: Who elects the Speaker of the state legislative assembly?

options.b: The assembly itself from amongst its members

faqs.a: The assembly itself from amongst its members

faqs.q: A resolution to remove the Speaker of the assembly can be moved only after giving how many days' advance notice?
A resolution to remove the Speaker must be passed by what kind of majority?
faqs.e: This means a majority of all the then members of the assembly.

faqs.q: The Speaker of the assembly resigns by writing to whom?
Which of the following powers is exercised by the Speaker but NOT by the Chairman of the Legislative Council?

options.a: Exercising a casting vote in case of a tie
options.b: Adjourning the House in absence of quorum
options.c: Deciding whether a bill is a Money Bill
options.d: Maintaining order and decorum in the House

faqs.a: Deciding whether a bill is a Money Bill
faqs.e: The Speaker's decision on whether a bill is a Money Bill is final; this special power is not enjoyed by the Chairman of the council.

faqs.q: The Speaker does not vote in the first instance but may exercise what kind of vote in case of a tie?
The Speaker is the chairman of which of the following committees of the assembly?
faqs.e: The Speaker is also chairman of the Rules Committee and the General Purpose Committee.

faqs.q: The Deputy Speaker of the assembly is elected after the election of whom has taken place?
The Deputy Speaker resigns by writing to whom?
The panel of chairman for the assembly, who may preside in the absence of both the Speaker and Deputy Speaker, is nominated by whom?
The salaries and allowances of the Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Chairman and Deputy Chairman are charged on which fund, making them not subject to annual vote?
Who elects the Chairman of the legislative council?

options.d: The council itself from amongst its members

faqs.a: The council itself from amongst its members

faqs.q: The panel of vice-chairman for the council, who may preside in the absence of both the Chairman and Deputy Chairman, is nominated by whom?
What is the maximum permissible gap between two sessions of the state legislature?
faqs.e: This means the state legislature must meet at least twice a year.

faqs.q: Who has the power to summon each House of the state legislature to meet?
Termination of a sitting of the state legislature for an indefinite period is termed what?
The power of adjournment, including adjournment sine die, lies with whom?

options.c: The presiding officer of the House

faqs.a: The presiding officer of the House

faqs.q: Unlike an adjournment, a prorogation terminates what?

options.b: The life of the House permanently

faqs.q: Which House of the state legislature is subject to dissolution?
On dissolution of the assembly, what happens to a bill pending in the assembly?

options.a: It is reserved for the President
options.b: It is transferred to the council

faqs.e: This applies whether the bill originated in the assembly or was transmitted to it by the council.

faqs.q: On dissolution of the assembly, does a bill passed by the assembly but pending assent of the Governor or President lapse?

options.c: Only if pending for more than six months
options.d: Only if it is a money bill

faqs.q: What is the quorum required to transact business in a House of the state legislature?

options.a: Twenty members or one-fifth of total membership, whichever is greater
options.b: Ten members or one-tenth of total membership, whichever is greater
options.c: A simple majority of total membership
options.d: Five members or one-twentieth of total membership, whichever is greater

faqs.a: Ten members or one-tenth of total membership, whichever is greater

faqs.q: If there is no quorum during a meeting, it is the duty of the presiding officer to do what?

options.b: Refer the matter to the Governor
options.d: Adjourn the House or suspend the meeting until there is a quorum

faqs.a: Adjourn the House or suspend the meeting until there is a quorum

faqs.q: All matters at any sitting of either House are decided by what kind of majority of members present and voting, excluding the presiding officer?

options.a: Effective majority as a default rule
options.b: Simple majority as a default rule
options.c: Two-thirds majority as a default rule
options.d: Special majority as a default rule

faqs.a: Simple majority as a default rule
faqs.e: Only a few matters specifically mentioned in the Constitution require effective majority or special majority.

faqs.q: The state legislature was authorised to decide whether to continue or discontinue English as a floor language after how many years from the commencement of the Constitution, i.e., from 1965?
For Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya and Tripura, the time limit for continuing English as a floor language was fixed at how many years?
For Arunachal Pradesh, Goa and Mizoram, the time limit for continuing English as a floor language was fixed at how many years?
Every minister and the Advocate General of the state have the right to speak and take part in proceedings of either House, but are subject to what restriction?

options.a: They can only speak on financial bills
options.b: They are not entitled to vote
options.c: They cannot address more than twice per session
options.d: They must be members of at least one House

faqs.a: They are not entitled to vote

faqs.q: An ordinary bill can be introduced in a bicameral state legislature by whom?

options.c: Either a minister or any other member

faqs.a: Either a minister or any other member

faqs.q: An ordinary bill passes through how many stages (readings) in the originating House?
faqs.e: These are the first reading, second reading, and third reading.

faqs.q: In a unicameral state legislature, a bill passed by the assembly is sent directly to whom for assent?
When a bill passed by the assembly is transmitted to the council, how many alternatives does the council have before it?
faqs.e: These are: pass without amendments, pass with amendments and return for reconsideration, reject altogether, or take no action and keep it pending.

faqs.q: At most, for how long can the legislative council detain or delay an ordinary bill passed by the assembly?
faqs.e: This is three months in the first instance and one month in the second instance.

faqs.q: If the council does not take any action on a bill for three months, what may the assembly do?

options.c: Pass the bill again and transmit it to the council
options.d: Directly send the bill to the Governor bypassing the council

faqs.a: Pass the bill again and transmit it to the council

faqs.q: Does the Constitution provide for a joint sitting mechanism to resolve a deadlock between the two Houses of a state legislature over an ordinary bill?

options.d: No, such a mechanism does not exist

faqs.a: No, such a mechanism does not exist

faqs.q: If an ordinary bill originates in the council, is sent to the assembly, and is rejected by the assembly, what happens to the bill?

options.b: It is automatically reserved for the President
options.c: It returns to the council for reconsideration
options.d: It is referred to a joint committee

faqs.q: When the Governor returns a bill for reconsideration and it is passed again by the House(s) with or without amendments, what is the Governor's obligation?

options.a: The Governor may return it again for reconsideration
options.b: The Governor may still withhold assent
options.c: The Governor must give assent to the bill
options.d: The Governor must reserve it for the President

faqs.a: The Governor must give assent to the bill
faqs.e: This means the Governor enjoys only a suspensive veto with respect to ordinary bills, the same position as at the Centre.

faqs.q: When the President returns a bill reserved by the Governor for reconsideration of the state legislature, within what period must the House(s) reconsider it?
Is it obligatory under the Constitution for the President to give assent to a bill presented again after reconsideration following reservation by the Governor?

options.b: No, this is not specified in the Constitution
options.d: Only if it is a money bill

faqs.a: No, this is not specified in the Constitution

faqs.q: A Money Bill can be introduced in the state legislature only in which House?

options.b: Either House at the introducer's choice

faqs.q: A Money Bill can be introduced only on whose recommendation, and only by whom?

options.a: The Speaker's recommendation, by any member
options.b: The Chief Minister's recommendation, by any member
options.c: The President's recommendation, by a minister
options.d: The Governor's recommendation, by a minister

faqs.a: The Governor's recommendation, by a minister

faqs.q: After a Money Bill is passed by the assembly and transmitted to the council, within how many days must the council return it?
Can the legislative council reject or amend a Money Bill?

options.a: Yes, it can reject but not amend
options.b: Yes, it can amend but not reject
options.c: Yes, it has full powers equal to the assembly
options.d: No, it can only make recommendations

faqs.a: No, it can only make recommendations

faqs.q: If the council does not return a Money Bill to the assembly within 14 days, what is deemed to have happened?

options.a: The bill is automatically reserved for the President
options.b: The bill is deemed passed by both Houses in the form originally passed by the assembly

faqs.a: The bill is deemed passed by both Houses in the form originally passed by the assembly

faqs.q: When a Money Bill is presented to the Governor, which alternative is NOT available to him/her?

options.a: Reserve the bill for the President's consideration
options.b: Return the bill for reconsideration of the state legislature

faqs.a: Return the bill for reconsideration of the state legislature

faqs.q: As per the Sarkaria Commission's classification, a bill which so derogates from the powers of the High Court as to endanger its constitutional position must be reserved for the President's consideration under which Article?

As per the Sarkaria Commission's classification, a bill relating to the imposition of taxes on water or electricity in certain cases attracts the provisions of which Article, requiring mandatory reservation for the President?

As per the Sarkaria Commission's classification, bills relating to acquisition of estates, intended to secure immunity from Articles 14 and 19, may be reserved for the President's consideration under which Article?
faqs.e: Bills giving effect to certain Directive Principles of State Policy for the same immunity purpose fall under Article 31C.

faqs.q: A bill relating to a subject in the Concurrent List, reserved for the President to secure operation despite repugnancy to a Union law, falls under which Article?
A bill imposing restrictions on trade and commerce, requiring prior Presidential sanction not earlier obtained, relates to which Article?
Unlike the Rajya Sabha at the Centre, does the Constitution provide for a joint sitting mechanism to resolve deadlocks between the two Houses of a state legislature over ordinary bills?

options.a: Only for bills originating in the council
options.b: Only during a state of emergency
options.c: No, no such mechanism exists at the state level

faqs.a: No, no such mechanism exists at the state level

faqs.q: At the Centre, can the Lok Sabha override the Rajya Sabha on an ordinary bill by passing it a second time?

options.d: No, only a joint sitting can resolve such a deadlock

faqs.a: No, only a joint sitting can resolve such a deadlock
faqs.e: In contrast, at the state level, the legislative assembly can override the legislative council by passing the bill a second time.

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements comparing the deadlock mechanism for ordinary bills at the Centre and in the states:
(I) At the Centre, the mechanism of joint sitting applies to a bill originating in either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha
(II) At the state level, the mechanism of passing the bill a second time applies only to a bill originating in the legislative assembly
(III) At the state level, if a bill originating in the council is rejected by the assembly, the bill ends and becomes dead
Which of the above is/are correct?
With regard to money bills, both at the Centre and in the states, within how many days must the second House return the bill with or without recommendations?
Regarding resolution of deadlocks over money bills, why does the Constitution not provide any resolution mechanism at either the Centre or the state level?

options.a: Because money bills cannot cause deadlocks by definition
options.b: Because the will of the lower House (Lok Sabha/assembly) is made to prevail over that of the upper House (Rajya Sabha/council)
options.c: Because money bills always require a joint sitting
options.d: Because money bills lapse automatically if delayed

faqs.a: Because the will of the lower House (Lok Sabha/assembly) is made to prevail over that of the upper House (Rajya Sabha/council)

faqs.q: In which sphere are the powers and status of the legislative council broadly equal to that of the assembly?

options.b: Approval of ordinances issued by the Governor
options.c: Removal of the council of ministers

faqs.a: Approval of ordinances issued by the Governor

faqs.q: Ministers, including the Chief Minister, can be members of either House of the state legislature, but are responsible only to which House?
Which of the following powers is exclusively vested in the legislative assembly and NOT shared with the council?

options.a: Considering reports of the State Finance Commission
options.d: Approving ordinances issued by the Governor

faqs.e: The council can only discuss the budget but cannot vote on the demands for grants.

faqs.q: Can the legislative council remove the council of ministers by passing a no-confidence motion?

options.a: Yes, it has equal power with the assembly in this regard
options.b: No, since the council of ministers is collectively responsible only to the assembly
options.d: Only if the Chief Minister belongs to the council

faqs.a: No, since the council of ministers is collectively responsible only to the assembly

faqs.q: The legislative council does not participate in the election of which two constitutional functionaries/bodies?

options.c: The Advocate General and State Election Commissioner
options.d: The President of India and representatives of the state in the Rajya Sabha

faqs.a: The President of India and representatives of the state in the Rajya Sabha

faqs.q: Whose will prevails over the council's in the ratification of a constitutional amendment bill by a state legislature?
The very existence of the legislative council depends on the will of which body, since it can be abolished by Parliament on that body's recommendation?
The pattern of relationship between the two Houses of a state legislature, where the council must yield to the assembly, is adopted from which model?
faqs.e: In Britain, the House of Lords cannot oppose and obstruct the House of Commons and can only delay bills.

faqs.q: In Britain's House of Lords model, for how long can an ordinary bill be delayed at most?
faqs.e: A money bill can be delayed for only one month.

faqs.q: Critics have described the weak and insignificant legislative council using which of the following terms?
Which of the following is cited as a ground supporting the utility of the legislative council despite its lesser powers?

options.a: It has equal power to pass money bills
options.c: It can dismiss the council of ministers when needed
options.d: It facilitates representation of eminent professionals and experts who cannot face direct elections

faqs.a: It facilitates representation of eminent professionals and experts who cannot face direct elections

faqs.q: To whom has the Constitution extended the privileges of the state legislature, apart from members, among persons entitled to speak in its proceedings?

options.c: The Advocate General and state ministers

faqs.a: The Advocate General and state ministers

faqs.q: Do the privileges of the state legislature extend to the Governor, who is also an integral part of the state legislature?

options.a: No, they do not extend to the Governor

faqs.a: No, they do not extend to the Governor

faqs.q: Which of the following is a collective privilege enjoyed by each House of the state legislature?

options.a: Immunity from arrest at all times
options.c: The right to publish its reports, debates and proceedings and to prohibit others from publishing the same
options.d: Freedom from all forms of legal process

faqs.a: The right to publish its reports, debates and proceedings and to prohibit others from publishing the same
faqs.e: The 44th Amendment Act of 1978 restored the press's freedom to publish true reports of state legislature proceedings without prior permission, except for secret sittings.

faqs.q: As a collective privilege, no legal process can be served within the precincts of the House without whose permission?
As an individual privilege, members cannot be arrested during the session and for how many days before and after such session?
faqs.e: This privilege applies only in civil cases, not in criminal cases or preventive detention cases.

faqs.q: The individual privilege of freedom of speech for a member of the state legislature is subject to what?

options.a: The provisions of the Constitution and the rules and standing orders regulating procedure

faqs.a: The provisions of the Constitution and the rules and standing orders regulating procedure
faqs.e: Article 211 additionally bars discussion in the state legislature on the conduct of any Supreme Court or High Court judge in discharge of duties.
